executiveSummary: Five AI deployments run across four systems, and the two facts worth the board's time are both about change rather than about models. Contoso re-based the assistant that screens job applicants onto a different foundation model in June and left the product version number unchanged; every answer in our April assessment was about a different model, and nothing except this register noticed. Separately, a writing tool nobody approved is drafting customer-facing proposals — found in a CASB review in May, in this register the same day, and still in use. Neither is a failure of a control. Both are the same gap: things change under us faster than the cycle that looks at them.

deployments.D-001: Screens job applicants and produces the decision, on regulated personal data. It is the most assessed thing here — a red-team report, a signed no-training commitment, controls recorded against integrity and privacy — and the assessment was made against a base model the provider has since replaced. What we know about it is real and is now a quarter out of date.
deployments.D-002: Drafts marketing copy on the same assistant. A person edits everything before it leaves, so it is the one deployment here where the low level is the whole story.
deployments.D-003: Scores churn for the renewals desk, who work the list every morning. It has not been assessed since June last year, which is past the annual cadence for its level.
deployments.D-004: Auto-remediates low-severity tickets without a person in the loop. It was assessed in March against two connected systems; it reaches three now, and the third is the change queue. What a deployment can reach is what bounds the damage, so it was assessed as a smaller thing than the one running today.
deployments.D-005: Drafts customer-facing proposals on a tool nobody sanctioned, found in a CASB egress review in May. Nobody has declared what it supports, so its criticality is untraced rather than low — we cannot yet say what would be affected if it were wrong, and it is writing to customers.

decisions.text: Have the owner of the shadow writing deployment declare what it supports, so the next review can place it rather than reporting it as untraced.
Re-assess the auto-remediation deployment against the three systems it now reaches, rather than the two it was assessed against.
